column1: # Example sentences for the claim guard's form tables (tests/test_ledger_claims.py).
# Every form in STRONG_FORMS / LEDGER_FORMS must own at least one row here; the named form alone
# must match its example, no other form on the same side may, and the example must also match the
# other side (it is a claim as the enumerator defines one). test_guard_forms_are_exampled enforces
# all of that, and test_deleting_any_form_breaks_its_example drills each form's removal. These are
# synthetic sentences written for the fixture; they state nothing about the shipped ledger.

column3: Every wrapped sentence is keyed whole.
All split sentences are joined first.
Each row is pinned to its primary.
None of the rows is a bound.
A row is never composed through an arbitrary factor.
The tier median is always taken over the same rows.
Only one row states its useful fraction.
The sole pinned row of its tier is the design study.
The figure rests solely on the ledger's own rows.
The locator is exact for the row.
The row's numeraire is unique within its tier.
The chain point is uniquely determined by the row.
Neither row reaches the terminal stage.
Any row may be read off the ledger.
The entire ledger is read at load time.
No row is a mean of two readings.
Nothing in the ledger is fitted.
Every anchor is read from the primary.
All anchors are read from the primary.
Each source is cited with a locator.
The chain is never composed twice.
No two chains share a factor.
The headline is never a mean.
All values are read from the primary.
All numbers are read from the primary.
The spread is never a measurement.
